page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-64 is a high-memory compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 virtual CPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache architecture provides 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 55 MB shared L3 cache. System memory measures 416.0 GB RAM, delivering an allocation of 6.5 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core processing places in the bottom quartile across standard suites, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 952.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1116.79. Multi-threaded processing leverages the 64 vCPUs to achieve mid-tier ratings, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 9803.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 36153.74. The memory subsystem delivers 80.73 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block reads and 31.32 GB/sec in write operations. In operational workloads, the instance sustained 39.4 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs center on memory volume versus instruction support and per-core speed. The CPU architecture lacks AVX-512, AMX, and modern vector extensions, resulting in constrained performance for dense mathematical computations and large language model inference. However, the high memory density makes the platform cost-efficient for applications where large working sets reside entirely in RAM without requiring high single-core compute performance. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases, Redis cache layers, ETL pipelines, multi-threaded compilation, and large enterprise reporting jobs.
